1.4. **"General Body"** means the body of all members of the Association in good standing.

1.5. **"Managing Committee"** means the committee elected by the General Body to manage the day-to-day affairs of the Association.

1.6. **"Office Bearers"** means the President, Vice-President, Secretary, Joint Secretary, Treasurer and such other office bearers as may be elected from time to time.

1.7. **"Common Areas"** means all areas within the complex not forming part of any individual member unit, including but not limited to the club house, swimming pool, gymnasium, children's play area, internal roads, footpaths, gardens, open spaces, lifts, staircases, corridors, service ducts, transformer room, pump house, sewage treatment plant and any other facilities designated as common by the Association.

1.8. **"Year"** means the financial year commencing on the 1st day of April and ending on the 31st day of March of the following year.

1.9. **"Financial Year"** shall have the same meaning as "Year" defined above.

1.10. **"Good Standing"** means a member who has paid all dues, charges, levies and contributions payable to the Association, and who is not in arrears of any sum due to the Association, and who has not been suspended from membership.

1.11. **"Written Notice"** means a notice given in writing, either by hand delivery, by post, or by electronic communication to the last known address or email address of the member.

---

**ARTICLE II: MEMBERSHIP**

2.1. **Eligibility for Membership**

a) Any person who is the owner of a member unit within Shanti Vihar shall be eligible to become a member of the Association.

According to the bye-laws, the annual general meeting quorum for Shanti Vihar RWA is 10% of total members. Record status: current.

b) In case of joint ownership, the joint owners shall jointly nominate one person to be the member of the Association for that member unit. Such nomination shall be in writing and signed by all joint owners.

c) A tenant or lessee shall not be eligible for membership, unless specifically permitted by the Managing Committee in exceptional circumstances, and such permission shall not confer voting rights.

2.2. **Admission to Membership**

a) Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form, accompanied by the applicable admission fee and the first year's subscription, if any.

b) The Managing Committee shall consider each application and may admit or reject the same at its discretion. The decision of the Managing Committee shall be final and binding.

c) Upon admission, the applicant's name shall be entered in the Register of Members, and a membership card shall be issued.

2.3. **Categories of Membership**

a) **Ordinary Member:** Any person who is the owner of a member unit and has been admitted as a member shall be an Ordinary Member. Ordinary Members shall have the right to vote at meetings of the General Body.

b) **Associate Member:** A tenant or lessee, or any other person permitted by the Managing Committee, may be admitted as an Associate Member. Associate Members shall not have the right to vote, but may attend meetings of the General Body as observers.

c) **Honorary Member:** The General Body may, by a resolution passed by a simple majority, confer honorary membership on any person who has rendered distinguished service to the Association or to the community. Honorary Members shall not have the right to vote.

2.4. **Cessation of Membership**

a) Membership shall cease upon:
   i) Transfer of ownership of the member unit by the member;
   ii) Death of the member, unless the legal heir applies for and is granted membership in accordance with these Bye-laws;
   iii) Resignation in writing to the Secretary;
   iv) Expulsion in accordance with Bye-law 2.6.
b) The ground floor of Tower B includes a community hall, which may be booked by members for private functions and events, subject to payment of such charges as may be fixed by the Managing Committee and compliance with the rules governing the use of the hall. The hall shall be available for use between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., unless extended by the Managing Committee for a specific occasion.

c) Tower B also houses a children's play area on the ground floor, adjacent to the community hall. The play area shall be maintained by the Association, and members are requested to supervise their children while they are using the play area.

**3.4. Tower C**

a) Tower C is a high-rise residential building consisting of ground floor plus twelve upper floors. The number of flats in Tower C is 120, with each floor containing nine residential units of varying configurations, including one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom units. This number is current as of the date of these Bye-laws and shall be updated only upon a formal amendment duly passed by the General Body in accordance with Bye-law 13.

b) The ground floor of Tower C comprises the main entrance lobby, a mailroom, and a small convenience store area, which may be leased out by the Managing Committee with the prior approval of the General Body. The terms of any such lease shall be reported to the General Body at its next meeting.

c) The terrace of Tower C is equipped with a solar water heating system, which supplements the central hot water supply for the building. The maintenance of this system shall be the responsibility of the Association.

**3.5. Common Areas and Amenities**

The number of flats in Tower C is 120. Record status: current.

a) The common areas of the complex shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
   i) All entrance lobbies, corridors, staircases, and lift lobbies;
   ii) The boundary walls, gates, and security cabins;
   iii) The internal roads, pathways, and pavements within the complex;
   iv) The landscaped gardens, lawns, and open spaces;
   v) The clubhouse, swimming pool, gymnasium, and other recreational facilities;
   vi) The sewage treatment plant, water treatment plant, and other utility installations;
   vii) The transformer room, generator room, and electrical distribution panels;
   viii) The fire-fighting equipment and systems, including fire hydrants and sprinkler systems.

b) The Association shall be responsible for the upkeep, repair, and maintenance of all common areas and amenities, and shall levy such maintenance charges on members as may be determined by the Managing Committee from time to time, subject to the approval of the General Body.

**3.6. Parking**

a) Parking spaces within the complex are allotted to members on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to availability and the payment of the prescribed parking charges. The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of all parking allotments, indicating the member unit, the vehicle registration number, and the parking space allotted.

b) Each member unit in Tower A and Tower B is entitled to one covered parking space. Each member unit in Tower C is entitled to one covered parking space, and the remaining covered parking spaces in Tower C may be allotted to members of other towers on a payment basis, if available.

c) Visitor parking is provided at designated areas near the main entrance of each tower. Visitors shall park only in the designated visitor parking areas and shall display a visitor pass issued by the security staff. The Association shall not be responsible for any damage to or loss of vehicles parked in the common areas.

d) No member shall park any vehicle in a manner that obstructs the movement of other vehicles, blocks the entrance or exit of any tower, or occupies a parking space not allotted to that member. The Managing Committee may, in the event of a violation, cause the vehicle to be towed away at the owner's risk and cost.
b) The Managing Committee shall cause a maintenance schedule to be prepared for all major equipment and installations, including but not limited to lifts, generators, water pumps, sewage treatment plant, and fire-fighting systems. The maintenance schedule shall be displayed on the notice board and circulated to members, and the Managing Committee shall ensure that the said schedule is adhered to.

c) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of all maintenance works carried out in the complex, indicating the date of the work, the nature of the work, the name of the contractor or agency, and the cost incurred. The register shall be open for inspection by any member at reasonable hours.

**4.3. Utilities and Services**

a) The Association shall make arrangements for the supply of water, electricity, and other essential services to the members, either through the concerned authorities or through its own arrangements, as may be necessary.

b) In the event of any disruption or failure of any utility or service, the Managing Committee shall take all reasonable steps to restore the same at the earliest, and shall keep the members informed of the progress of the restoration work.

c) The Managing Committee may, from time to time, impose such charges for the use of any utility or service, or for the consumption of water or electricity in excess of the normal entitlement, as may be determined by the General Body.

**4.4. Defect Liability Period**

a) The original builder of the complex, Horizon Developers Ltd., had provided a defect liability period in respect of the construction of the complex, as per the terms of the original builder agreement. The defect liability period end for Horizon Developers is 2018-03-31, and the said period is now historical and has lapsed. Any defects or deficiencies in the construction of the complex which have not been attended to by the said builder within the said period shall be the responsibility of the Association, and the Association shall take appropriate action to rectify the same at its own cost.

The defect liability period end for Horizon Developers is 2018-03-31. Record status: historical.

b) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of all defects or deficiencies reported by members during the defect liability period, indicating the date of the complaint, the nature of the defect, the action taken by the builder, and the date of completion of the said action. The register shall be preserved as a permanent record of the Association.

c) For the avoidance of doubt, it is clarified that the provisions of this clause are without prejudice to any other rights or remedies that the Association or any member may have against the builder under any law for the time being in force.

**4.5. Warranty on Common Area Equipment**

a) In respect of equipment and installations in the common areas which are covered by any warranty provided by the manufacturer or supplier, the Managing Committee shall ensure that the terms of such warranty are complied with, and that the equipment is serviced and maintained as per the manufacturer's guidelines.

b) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of all warranties, indicating the equipment, the name of the manufacturer or supplier, the date of commencement of the warranty, the date of expiry of the warranty, and the terms and conditions of the warranty. The register shall be placed before the General Body at its annual meeting.

c) In the event of any dispute with the manufacturer or supplier regarding the warranty, the Managing Committee shall take all reasonable steps to resolve the dispute, and may, if necessary, refer the matter to the appropriate consumer forum or other authority.

**4.6. Dispute Resolution**
**5. USE AND MAINTENANCE OF COMMON AREAS AND FACILITIES**

**5.1. Community Hall**

a) The community hall located on the ground floor of Block B, admeasuring approximately 1,200 square feet, shall be available for use by members for social, cultural, religious, and family functions, subject to the provisions of this clause and the rules framed by the Managing Committee from time to time.

b) Any member desiring to book the community hall shall apply in writing to the Secretary at least fifteen (15) days in advance, in the form prescribed by the Managing Committee. The application shall state the date, time, and nature of the function.

c) The hall shall be allotted on a first-come, first-served basis, provided that no more than two (2) bookings shall be accepted for any single day. In the event of a clash, the Managing Committee shall resolve the same by drawing lots.

d) The charges for the use of the community hall shall be as fixed by the General Body from time to time. The current charges are as follows:

| Purpose | Charges per day |
|---------|-----------------|
| Members (Residents) | ₹2,000 |
| Non-resident owners | ₹3,000 |
| Security deposit (refundable) | ₹5,000 |

e) The security deposit shall be refunded within seven (7) days of the conclusion of the function, after deducting the cost of any damage caused to the hall, furniture, fittings, or equipment, as determined by the Managing Committee.

f) The member booking the hall shall be responsible for the conduct of all persons attending the function and shall ensure that:
   i. The noise level is kept within reasonable limits and that no disturbance is caused to other residents;
   ii. The function concludes by 10:00 p.m. on weekdays and 11:00 p.m. on weekends and public holidays;
   iii. No cooking is done inside the hall except in the designated kitchen area;
   iv. The hall is left in a clean and tidy condition, and all garbage is removed and disposed of in the designated bins;
   v. No nails, screws, or other fixtures are driven into the walls, floor, or ceiling of the hall without prior written permission of the Managing Committee.

g) The Managing Committee may, at its discretion, waive the charges for the use of the community hall for functions organized by the Association itself or for charitable purposes.

h) The use of the community hall for commercial purposes, including but not limited to exhibitions, sales, or business meetings, is strictly prohibited unless specifically permitted by the General Body.

i) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of bookings, indicating the name of the member, the date of the function, the purpose, the charges collected, and the condition of the hall before and after the function.

**5.2. Pet Policy**

a) Members may keep domestic pets such as dogs, cats, birds, and fish in their flats, subject to the provisions of this clause and any applicable laws, rules, or regulations of the municipal authority or other statutory body.

b) No member shall keep any animal which is wild, dangerous, or prohibited by law, or which, in the opinion of the Managing Committee, poses a threat to the safety or health of other residents.

c) Members keeping pets shall ensure that:
   i. The pet is vaccinated as per the schedule prescribed by a qualified veterinary doctor, and the vaccination record is maintained and produced to the Managing Committee on request;
   ii. The pet is not allowed to roam freely in the common areas, corridors, staircases, lifts, or the compound, and is always kept on a leash or in a carrier when taken out of the flat;
   iii. The pet is not allowed to cause nuisance by way of excessive barking, howling, or other noise, particularly during the night hours;
   iv. The pet is not allowed to defecate or urinate in the common areas, and any accidental soiling is immediately cleaned up by the member or the person in charge of the pet;
   v. The pet is not allowed to enter the children's play area, the community hall, or the clubhouse, if any.

1.1 "Effective Date" shall mean the date of commencement of services as specified in Clause 2.1 herein.

**ARTICLE II: MEMBERSHIP**

2.1. **Eligibility for Membership**

a) Any person who is the owner of a member unit within Shanti Vihar shall be eligible to become a member of the Association.

According to the bye-laws, the annual general meeting quorum for Shanti Vihar RWA is 10% of total members. Record status: current.

b) In case of joint ownership, the joint owners shall jointly nominate one person to be the member of the Association for that member unit. Such nomination shall be in writing and signed by all joint owners.

c) A tenant or lessee shall not be eligible for membership, unless specifically permitted by the Managing Committee in exceptional circumstances, and such permission shall not confer voting rights.

2.2. **Admission to Membership**

a) Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form, accompanied by the applicable admission fee and the first year's subscription, if any.

b) The Managing Committee shall consider each application and may admit or reject the same at its discretion. The decision of the Managing Committee shall be final and binding.

c) Upon admission, the applicant's name shall be entered in the Register of Members, and a membership card shall be issued.

2.3. **Categories of Membership**

a) **Ordinary Member:** Any person who is the owner of a member unit and has been admitted as a member shall be an Ordinary Member. Ordinary Members shall have the right to vote at meetings of the General Body.

b) **Associate Member:** A tenant or lessee, or any other person permitted by the Managing Committee, may be admitted as an Associate Member. Associate Members shall not have the right to vote, but may attend meetings of the General Body as observers.

c) **Honorary Member:** The General Body may, by a resolution passed by a simple majority, confer honorary membership on any person who has rendered distinguished service to the Association or to the community. Honorary Members shall not have the right to vote.

2.4. **Cessation of Membership**

a) Membership shall cease upon:
   i) Transfer of ownership of the member unit by the member;
   ii) Death of the member, unless the legal heir applies for and is granted membership in accordance with these Bye-laws;
   iii) Resignation in writing to the Secretary;
   iv) Expulsion in accordance with Bye-law 2.6.

**5. USE AND MAINTENANCE OF COMMON AREAS AND FACILITIES**

**5.1. Community Hall**

a) The community hall located on the ground floor of Block B, admeasuring approximately 1,200 square feet, shall be available for use by members for social, cultural, religious, and family functions, subject to the provisions of this clause and the rules framed by the Managing Committee from time to time.

b) Any member desiring to book the community hall shall apply in writing to the Secretary at least fifteen (15) days in advance, in the form prescribed by the Managing Committee. The application shall state the date, time, and nature of the function.

c) The hall shall be allotted on a first-come, first-served basis, provided that no more than two (2) bookings shall be accepted for any single day. In the event of a clash, the Managing Committee shall resolve the same by drawing lots.

d) The charges for the use of the community hall shall be as fixed by the General Body from time to time. The current charges are as follows:

| Purpose | Charges per day |
|---------|-----------------|
| Members (Residents) | ₹2,000 |
| Non-resident owners | ₹3,000 |
| Security deposit (refundable) | ₹5,000 |

e) The security deposit shall be refunded within seven (7) days of the conclusion of the function, after deducting the cost of any damage caused to the hall, furniture, fittings, or equipment, as determined by the Managing Committee.

f) The member booking the hall shall be responsible for the conduct of all persons attending the function and shall ensure that:
   i. The noise level is kept within reasonable limits and that no disturbance is caused to other residents;
   ii. The function concludes by 10:00 p.m. on weekdays and 11:00 p.m. on weekends and public holidays;
   iii. No cooking is done inside the hall except in the designated kitchen area;
   iv. The hall is left in a clean and tidy condition, and all garbage is removed and disposed of in the designated bins;
   v. No nails, screws, or other fixtures are driven into the walls, floor, or ceiling of the hall without prior written permission of the Managing Committee.

g) The Managing Committee may, at its discretion, waive the charges for the use of the community hall for functions organized by the Association itself or for charitable purposes.

h) The use of the community hall for commercial purposes, including but not limited to exhibitions, sales, or business meetings, is strictly prohibited unless specifically permitted by the General Body.

i) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of bookings, indicating the name of the member, the date of the function, the purpose, the charges collected, and the condition of the hall before and after the function.

**5.2. Pet Policy**

a) Members may keep domestic pets such as dogs, cats, birds, and fish in their flats, subject to the provisions of this clause and any applicable laws, rules, or regulations of the municipal authority or other statutory body.

b) No member shall keep any animal which is wild, dangerous, or prohibited by law, or which, in the opinion of the Managing Committee, poses a threat to the safety or health of other residents.

c) Members keeping pets shall ensure that:
   i. The pet is vaccinated as per the schedule prescribed by a qualified veterinary doctor, and the vaccination record is maintained and produced to the Managing Committee on request;
   ii. The pet is not allowed to roam freely in the common areas, corridors, staircases, lifts, or the compound, and is always kept on a leash or in a carrier when taken out of the flat;
   iii. The pet is not allowed to cause nuisance by way of excessive barking, howling, or other noise, particularly during the night hours;
   iv. The pet is not allowed to defecate or urinate in the common areas, and any accidental soiling is immediately cleaned up by the member or the person in charge of the pet;
   v. The pet is not allowed to enter the children's play area, the community hall, or the clubhouse, if any.

**PREAMBLE**

This Service Agreement is entered into on the date of execution mentioned above, by and between the Association, acting through its duly elected Executive Committee, and the Service Provider. The Association is desirous of engaging the Service Provider for the provision of housekeeping, pest control, and solid waste management services for the common areas, amenities, and designated premises within the Nirmal Vihar Phase II complex, and the Service Provider has agreed to provide such services on the terms and conditions hereinafter appearing.

The parties agree as follows:

---

**1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION**

1.1 "Effective Date" shall mean the date of commencement of services as specified in Clause 2.1 herein.

1.2 "Common Areas" shall include all public and common spaces within the complex, including but not limited to, internal roads, footpaths, parks, lawns, community centre, clubhouse, lift lobbies, staircases, corridors, basement parking areas, service shafts, and the boundary walls.

1.3 "Services" shall mean the housekeeping, pest control, and solid waste management services as described in Annexure A, Annexure B, and Annexure C respectively.

1.4 "Authorised Representative" shall mean the person designated by each party in writing to communicate on their behalf regarding operational matters under this Agreement.

1.5 "Force Majeure" shall mean any event beyond the reasonable control of either party, including but not limited to, acts of God, war, riots, strikes, lockouts, fire, flood, earthquake, or any direction or order of any governmental authority.

---

**2. TERM AND COMMENCEMENT**

2.1 The Services shall commence on the Effective Date. The Effective Date and the term of this Agreement shall be as recorded in the Agreement Schedule attached hereto as Schedule I. The contract start date for Skyline Facilities is recorded as 2023-04-01. Record status: historical.

2.2 This Agreement shall remain in force for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the Effective Date, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement.

2.3 The parties may, by mutual written consent, extend the term of this Agreement for such additional period(s) and on such terms as may be agreed upon in writing.

---

**3. SCOPE OF SERVICES**

3.1 The Service Provider shall provide the Services in accordance with the detailed scope of work set out in Annexure A (Housekeeping), Annexure B (Pest Control), and Annexure C (Solid Waste Management).

3.2 The Service Provider shall deploy adequate and qualified personnel to perform the Services. The minimum number of personnel to be deployed at any given time shall be as specified in Annexure D.

3.3 All personnel deployed by the Service Provider shall be neatly attired in uniforms bearing the Service Provider's name/logo and shall carry valid identity cards issued by the Service Provider.

3.4 The Service Provider shall ensure that all its personnel are duly trained and competent to perform the assigned tasks. The Service Provider shall provide ongoing training as necessary.

3.5 The Service Provider shall comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and bye-laws in the performance of the Services.

---

**4. SERVICE LEVELS AND PERFORMANCE STANDARDS**

4.1 The Services shall be performed with due diligence and in accordance with the performance standards and frequency schedules specified in the respective Annexures.

4.2 The Association's Authorised Representative shall have the right to inspect the quality of Services at any reasonable time and shall record any deficiencies in the Inspection Register maintained for this purpose.

6.1 The Service Provider shall furnish, within fifteen (15) days of the Effective Date, an unconditional and irrevocable bank guarantee in favour of the Association, for an amount equivalent to three (3) months' charges, as security for the due performance of this Agreement.

**7. PENALTY AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES**

The contract end date for Skyline Facilities is 2026-03-31. Record status: current.

7.1 If the Service Provider fails to achieve the service levels or performance standards set out in the respective Annexures, the Association shall be entitled to recover liquidated damages from the Service Provider at the rates specified in Annexure F (Penalty Schedule). The rates specified therein are a genuine pre-estimate of the loss likely to be suffered by the Association and are not by way of penalty.

7.2 Without prejudice to the generality of Clause 7.1, the following penalties shall apply:
(a) Non-deployment of the minimum number of personnel: Rs. 500 per person per day of shortfall;

The decision of the Association's Authorised Representative, after considering the explanation, shall be final and binding.

(a) Material breach of any term of this Agreement, including but not limited to the service levels and performance standards, which remains unremedied for seven (7) days after receipt of a written notice;
(b) Fraud, corruption, or any act of moral turpitude by the Service Provider or its personnel;
(c) Insolvency, liquidation, or any analogous proceeding being initiated by or against the Service Provider;
(d) The Service Provider assigning, subletting, or otherwise transferring this Agreement or any part thereof without the prior written consent of the Association;
(e) Failure to maintain the minimum number of personnel for a continuous period of five (5) working days.

Mr. P. V. Rao, Treasurer, presented the audited income and expenditure statement for the financial year 2023-24 and the balance sheet as on 31st March 2024. He highlighted the following key points:

**14. Resolution: Appointment of Honorary Auditor for the Financial Year 2025-26**

The Executive Committee proposed the appointment of M/s. R. Ganesan & Associates, Chartered Accountants, as the Honorary Auditor for the financial year 2025-26. The firm has been associated with the Association for the past three years. The members present approved the appointment by a show of hands with 61 votes in favour, 3 against, and 4 abstentions. The term of the appointment shall be for one year, subject to renewal at the next AGM.

**15. Resolution: Approval of Revised Parking Norms for Visitor Vehicles**

A proposal was placed before the members to revise the parking norms for visitor vehicles, limiting the duration of visitor parking to 4 hours in the designated visitor bays. The proposal was discussed at length. Some members expressed concern about the adequacy of visitor parking spaces, especially during festive occasions. The members approved the revised norms with 55 votes in favour, 7 against, and 6 abstentions. The revised norms shall be communicated to all residents through the notice board and the resident WhatsApp group.

**16. Resolution: Installation of CCTV Cameras at the Main Gate and Clubhouse**

The Executive Committee proposed the installation of additional CCTV cameras at the main gate and the clubhouse premises. The estimated cost of the project is Rs. 2,40,000, which shall be met from the contingency reserve. The proposal was approved by the members present with 64 votes in favour, 2 against, and 2 abstentions. The Security Sub-committee shall invite quotations from at least three vendors and complete the installation within 60 days of the approval.

**17. Resolution: Adoption of Revised Housekeeping Schedule**

The Executive Committee placed a proposal to revise the housekeeping schedule for common areas, including the staircase, lifts, and the compound. The revised schedule shall include additional cleaning cycles during the monsoon season. The members present approved the revised schedule with 58 votes in favour, 5 against, and 5 abstentions. The revised schedule shall be displayed on the notice board and circulated to all residents.

**18. Resolution: Amendment to the Bye-laws regarding Pet Ownership**

A proposal was placed before the members to amend the bye-laws to regulate the ownership of pets within the premises. The proposed amendment includes the requirement of registration of pets with the Association and the prohibition of pets in the common areas without a leash. The amendment was discussed at length. Some members expressed concerns regarding the implementation of the same. The members approved the amendment with 52 votes in favour, 9 against, and 7 abstentions. The amended bye-law shall read as follows:

"All residents owning pets shall register the same with the Association within 15 days of the acquisition of the pet. Pets shall not be allowed in the common areas without a leash. The Executive Committee shall have the authority to impose a fine of Rs. 500 for the violation of this bye-law."

**19. Resolution: Approval of the Annual Report for the Financial Year 2024-25**

The Secretary presented the annual report for the financial year 2024-25, covering the activities and the financial performance of the Association. The report included a summary of the cultural events, the maintenance works carried out, and the financial statements. The members present approved the annual report with 63 votes in favour, 2 against, and 3 abstentions.

**20. Resolution: Proposal for the Construction of a Children's Play Area**

The Executive Committee proposed the construction of a children's play area in the open space near the clubhouse. The estimated cost of the project is Rs. 8,50,000. The proposal was discussed at length. Some members expressed concerns regarding the maintenance of the play area and the safety of the equipment. The members present approved the proposal with 57 votes in favour, 6 against, and 5 abstentions. The Executive Committee shall invite quotations from at least three vendors and complete the construction within 6 months of the approval.
